one-line thesis: Second consecutive quarter proving the trading→manufacturing pivot: blended EBITDA margin now >4% (~4.5%), annualized ROCE ~23%, on a net-cash Rs 690 cr balance sheet — with management stressing this is *structural*, not inventory-gain (absolute inventory actually fell to Rs 209 cr from Rs 284 cr despite Rs 2,500-3,000/ton steel-price inflation). The four value-added verticals (service centers, steel profiles, renewable structures, accessories) are being scaled toward a 2030 vision of 4-4.5 mn tons and Rs 25,000-35,000 cr revenue / Rs 1,000 cr+ EBITDA. The margin step-up lever is a Raipur backward-integration (coated-steel) line, operational in ~18 months, taking profile/renewable EBITDA/ton from Rs 3,000-4,000 to Rs 6,000-7,000.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service-center volume | 160,000 t | +33% YoY (vs ~120-121k) | QoQ dip = seasonality; Rs 1,800-2,000/t EBITDA |
| Steel-profiles volume | 18,000 t | — | ~75k t/yr run-rate; Rs 3,000-4,000/t EBITDA |
| Renewable-structures volume | 11,000 t | — | ~50k t/yr run-rate; Rs 3,000-3,500/t EBITDA |
| Blended EBITDA margin | >4% (~4.5%) | up | **structural, not inventory gain** |
| ROCE (annualized) | ~23% | — | group floor "no vertical below 20%" |
| Net cash | Rs 690 cr | — | funds capex; no dilution needed |
| Capex | Rs 90 cr (Q1) | — | FY27 Rs 400-500 cr; Rs 1,500 cr over 2-3 yrs |
| Inventory | Rs 209 cr | down from Rs 284 cr (Mar-26) | WC 27 days; churn improving despite +steel prices |
> Revenue not disclosed as a single figure on the call (volume-led disclosure). NSR rose on both steel-price inflation (+Rs 2,500-3,000/t Apr→Jun) *and* mix (special-coated profile/renewable products realize Rs 10,000-15,000/t above HR-coil base). Management explicitly wants to minimize inventory gain/loss noise ("like we did in APL Apollo").
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 EBITDA ~Rs 300 cr (absolute)** — reaffirmed from Q4 call; only caveat is a macro/geopolitical shock. Absolute EBITDA to grow every quarter (blended EBITDA/ton may wobble on mix).
- **Revenue growth ~50% CAGR** over next 3 years (analyst-stated, management-owned as target).
- **Service centers: 25 by 2029** (from 7; +5/yr); **12 operational within 6-12 months** (7 new already under construction, land/cities identified).
- **Raipur backward integration (coated steel): operational in ~18 months** → profile/renewable EBITDA/ton to Rs 6,000-7,000 (from Rs 3,000-4,000); +Rs 3,000-4,000/t uplift.
- **Profiles + renewables: 3.5-4x volume growth** in 2-3 years (120k t run-rate today vs 400k t installed capacity).
- **7 new products** to launch over Q2-Q3 FY27 (capacity already in place); new **contract-manufacturing** category — details next quarter.
- **Working capital: 27 days → 20-25 days** within 2 years (backward integration cuts raw-material stocking).
- **Vision 2030:** 4-4.5 mn tons; revenue Rs 25,000-35,000 cr; EBITDA min Rs 1,000 cr (3-4% margin) — 3 mn t service centers + ~1 mn t profiles/renewables, ~0 t trading.
order book & pipeline: Mostly off-the-shelf (24-48 hr turnaround) except solar structures (project-specific, 2-3 month order book). 2,500+ customers across EPC/industrial/infrastructure; concentration low except solar (top 20-30 EPCs/IPPs). Installed capacity 400,000 t (profiles+renewables) vs 120,000 t run-rate → 3.5-4x headroom. B2B trading kept optional/opportunistic (Q4 was only 17k t; "anyone's guess").
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Service Centers (7 operational):** SME/MSME customers (fabricators, capital goods, EPC, white goods, auto, agri-equipment); 8,000 t/month → ~Rs 40 cr revenue/month → ~Rs 500 cr/yr per center; Rs 50 cr gross-block + Rs 25-30 cr WC = Rs 75-80 cr capital/center → Rs 20 cr EBITDA; 9-15 months to build. ROCE can rise to ~35% once coated steel + B2B trading layer on.
- **Steel Profiles (18k t):** Strut, Z/C Purlins, racking, cable trays — construction/infra/industries; special-coated steel.
- **Renewable Structures (11k t):** solar module-mounting for EPCs/IPPs; capacity 200k t (2-3 yrs of demand headroom).
- **Accessories:** 2 products launched, double-digit margins; ramp begun.
- **B2B Metal Trading:** deliberately subordinate, zero-capital ROCE-booster.
growth verticals / optionality: Raipur coated-steel backward integration (CRM + zinc/zinc-al/zinc-al-mg coating); 7-product Q2-Q3 launch; contract manufacturing (new category, "gap in giving manufacturing ecosystem to brand-owners"); own online marketplace for SG Mart products; B2B trading optionality. Analogized as "China in the making" — multi-product/multi-industry/multi-channel formalization play.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Only pan-India *organized* service-center/profiling network:** competitors are fragmented "mom-and-pop" profilers buying from mills and selling locally; SGMART's edge is pan-India profiling at service centers **+ own backward integration** in coated steel — a combination "no existing player" in solar structures/profiles has. Multi-vertical/multi-channel breadth makes it "very tough for any big entrant."
- **APL Apollo DNA:** management explicitly runs the SG Mart playbook (inventory-churn discipline, minimize P&L inventory noise, value-added spread over volume) from its APL Apollo experience — a credible execution track record.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA/ton hierarchy: Accessories (double-digit %) > Profiles (Rs 3,000-4,000) ≈ Renewables (Rs 3,000-3,500) > Service Centers (Rs 1,800-2,000) > B2B trading. Blended >4% will oscillate with mix (a service-center-heavy quarter dilutes per-ton), but *absolute* EBITDA grows every quarter. Backward integration is the structural margin unlock (+Rs 3,000-4,000/t on profiles/renewables). Group ROCE floor: no vertical below 20%; aspiration >25%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Rs 90 cr Q1; Rs 400-500 cr FY27; Rs 1,500 cr total over 2-3 years — ~Rs 900 cr on 15-18 new service centers (Rs 50 cr each) + Raipur coated-steel line + accessories machinery. Fully funded by Rs 690 cr net cash + operating cash flow; **no capital raise / dilution**. Raipur land acquired, construction begun, some machinery ordered. **Watch:** service-center build cadence (12 within 6-12 months) + Raipur 18-month timeline.
capital allocation: Self-funded growth (net cash + OCF); no equity dilution. Discipline: any new vertical must clear >20% ROCE (contract manufacturing included). Working-capital rationalization (advances to mills to secure supply amid geopolitics) as scale builds.
risks & watch-items:
- **Geopolitics/steel-price volatility:** Iran-US war reignited ~10 days pre-call; oil→steel/commodity volatility; a March-style fuel/gas shortage would hurt customer industries and sales broadly ("nothing specific to us").
- **Coated-steel dependency** on third parties until Raipur commissions (18 months) — execution/slippage risk.
- **Seasonality** in service-center volumes (Q1 QoQ dip).
- **Mix-driven EBITDA/ton variability** (management won't guide per-ton QoQ).
- Rapid multi-vertical expansion execution risk.
management quality / tone: Confident, granular, disclosure-forward (added segmental splits; accepted analyst suggestion to publish per-segment EBITDA). Careful not to over-promise per-ton margins; reframes the "25 vs 30 service centers" target as coverage-of-industrial-clusters rather than a number. Repeatedly anchors credibility to the APL Apollo track record. Candid that a macro shock is the one real caveat to the Rs 300 cr EBITDA guide.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The margin uplift is *real*, not cyclical: absolute inventory fell Rs 284→209 cr into rising steel prices, so there is little inventory-gain flatter in the >4% EBITDA margin.
- Backward integration is the whole thesis — it converts a Rs 3,000-4,000/t bought-coated-steel business into a Rs 6,000-7,000/t integrated one; the 18-month Raipur timeline is the single most important milestone.
- Trading is being deliberately zeroed out of the 2030 volume vision (4 mn t of the target is "0 t trading") — a quality-over-volume signal often missed by those anchoring on the old aggregator model.
- Contract manufacturing (details next quarter) is a new, potentially large optionality not yet in numbers.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
